findings.name: Casual / Standard / Expert / Non-Stop ∞ Climax
findings.detail: Four difficulty tiers, easiest to hardest: Casual ('for those simply looking to enjoy the story'; scores not uploaded to rankings), Standard (default/recommended, 'traditional' experience), Expert ('for veterans of hardcore action'), and Non-Stop ∞ Climax (colloquially 'Infinite Climax') - the 'ultimate combat experience' with drastically tougher, stun-resistant enemies. Non-Stop ∞ Climax unlocks after clearing the story once on ANY difficulty (including Casual).
findings.trackable: Difficulty is selected from a 'Difficulty Select' menu (press + at the Chapter Select screen). No numeric completion percentage is tied to difficulty, but which difficulties have been cleared per chapter may be implied by medal records (unconfirmed).

findings.name: Difficulty is changeable per-chapter, not locked to a continuous playthrough
findings.detail: Unlike Bayonetta 1 and 2, difficulty in Bayonetta 3 can be changed at any time from the Chapter Select screen's menu (press +), not just at a New Game start. This applies to Casual/Standard/Expert and, once unlocked, very likely to Non-Stop ∞ Climax as well (multiple sources describe switching among 'casual, standard, and expert' freely and describe Infinite Climax as unlocked in the same Difficulty Select menu, implying the same free-switching applies to it).
findings.trackable: Not explicitly confirmed whether the game records/displays 'this chapter cleared on Non-Stop ∞ Climax' anywhere.
findings.notes: IMPORTANT for trophy design: a 'beat the game on Non-Stop ∞ Climax' trophy likely does NOT require an unbroken single continuous playthrough at that difficulty - a player could plausibly clear chapters individually at that difficulty via Chapter Select after initially finishing the story on Casual. Could not find a source that explicitly confirms or denies whether the game tracks a per-chapter 'highest difficulty cleared' flag, which would be needed to verify a 'full game on hardest difficulty' trophy is legitimately completable/verifiable rather than gameable via easier settings for most of the run.

findings.name: Verse medal ranks: Bronze / Silver / Gold / Platinum / Pure Platinum
findings.detail: The classic Bayonetta verse-rank system carries over into Bayonetta 3. After each Verse (combat encounter within a chapter), the game grades performance and awards a medal. Pure Platinum requires clearing the verse quickly, with big combos, and taking ZERO damage (even one point of damage caps the result at regular Platinum). A chapter's overall grade is derived by tallying medals across all its verses.
findings.trackable: Confirmed a post-verse completion screen shows the medal earned, per Scout D's Chapter 9 walkthrough source (enemy health bars + point-threshold challenges). Whether chapter select displays the CUMULATIVE/BEST medal per verse or per chapter (so a player can check 'did I get Pure Platinum on all verses' without replaying) was NOT independently confirmed this pass.
findings.notes: The 'Stone' rank (lowest tier in Bayonetta 1, given for dying 5+ times in a chapter) could NOT be confirmed to exist in Bayonetta 3 specifically - all Bayonetta-3-specific sources found only mention Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum/Pure Platinum (5 tiers, not 6). Treat 'Stone' as unconfirmed/possibly not present in BY3; do not assume the 6-tier BY1/2 system carried over unchanged.

findings.name: Medallion Shards (Blue Medallion) -> secret chapter 'The Artifact Unleashed' -> boss 'Golem'
findings.detail: CONFIRMED (this corrects an earlier low-confidence flag from a prior research pass). Four Medallion Shard fragments are hidden as unassuming/depowered treasure boxes across the campaign: in Chapter 1 (after Verse 1), Chapter 4 (after Verse 1, near sun/moon pillars), Chapter 7 (Ginnungagap portal zone), and Chapter 10 (after Verse 2, inside a breakable stone tower). Collecting all 4 assembles the Blue Medallion and unlocks a secret extra chapter, 'The Artifact Unleashed,' accessible via a green icon on the Chapter Select map. It contains a single-verse boss fight against a shapeshifting 'prismatic Golem' (mimics previously seen enemies + laser attacks). Reward: one full Witch Heart and one complete Moon Pearl.
findings.trackable: A green icon appears on the Chapter Select map once all 4 shards are collected, functioning as a visible unlock indicator (same pattern as the red Phenomenal Remnant icon).
findings.notes: Not permanently missable: shards are found in main-story chapters (1, 4, 7, 10) which remain replayable via Chapter Select indefinitely.

findings.name: No permanently missable content identified
findings.detail: Every collectible/challenge system checked this pass (Umbran Tears of Blood, Bewitchments, Card Packs, Figure Boxes, Medallion Shards) is located within main-story chapters, and chapters are confirmed replayable via Chapter Select at any time after first completion, including after finishing the whole game. No source found describing a point-of-no-return that locks a player out of any collectible, side mission, or optional boss.
sources: General search synthesis on chapter replay ('upon completing a chapter, players will be able to replay it at any time via the Chapter Select screen')
Scout D dossier (Umbran Tears: 'Chapters can be replayed to pick up missed tears')
findings.notes: This is an absence-of-evidence conclusion, not an explicit official statement that 'nothing is missable.' Recommend against building any 'permanently missable collectible' trophy for this game; series precedent (BY1/BY2) also had no permanently missable content once chapter select unlocks.

findings.name: No overall save-file / menu completion percentage found
findings.detail: Despite dedicated searching (including community 100%-save-file discussions on GBAtemp and Speedrun.com), no source describes a single aggregate completion percentage number anywhere in Bayonetta 3's UI. What DOES exist: per-chapter Bewitchment checklist (5 per chapter), per-chapter Umbran Tear of Blood indicator (3 per chapter, shown via icon), and presumably a Gallery menu tracking unlocked Card Pack / Figure Box art (not confirmed to show a numeric counter). Community members on GBAtemp explicitly discuss NOT having a true 100% save file readily available, suggesting completion is tracked player-side (via wikis) rather than via an official percentage.
findings.trackable: No aggregate percentage confirmed anywhere. Only itemized per-chapter checklists (Bewitchments, Umbran Tears) are confirmed to be displayed.
findings.notes: This remains the single most load-bearing gap for 'collect everything'-style trophies: without an in-game aggregate tracker, any 100%-completion trophy must be built from the sum of separately-tracked per-chapter checklists (Bewitchments + Umbran Tears), not a single UI number.

findings.name: Bayonetta, Viola, Jeanne (3 total)
findings.detail: Bayonetta and Viola are both playable across the main 14-chapter campaign (specific chapter-by-chapter split not fully itemized this pass, but Viola is confirmed to play a substantial portion). Jeanne is playable DURING the campaign only in limited contexts: her four numbered 'Side Mission' 2D stealth-action chapters, Phenomenal Remnant challenge chapters, and specific special encounters (e.g., fights against Rodin or the secret Golem boss). After completing the main story once (on ANY difficulty, including Casual), Jeanne is unlocked as a full playable character from the Main Menu and can play through the ENTIRE main story campaign as her, not just her side-content segments.
findings.trackable: Character select is available from the Main Menu post-completion; no separate per-character completion tracker confirmed.
findings.notes: Character-specific mechanic difference (from prior pass, still reliable): Viola cannot trigger Witch Time via a standard last-second dodge like Bayonetta; she must use a parry mechanic instead. This is directly relevant to any 'trigger Witch Time as Viola' trophy wording.

findings.name: Three on-screen currencies: Halos, Orbs, (Homunculus) Seeds
findings.detail: Bayonetta 3 displays three distinct currencies simultaneously in the top-right of the HUD: Halos (now a rarity, used exclusively for cosmetic items - found in hidden Verses vs. Angels or hidden in world objects), Orbs (earned via Combo Points in battle, used to level up Infernal Demons), and Seeds/Homunculus Seeds (the main currency, dropped by Homunculi enemies, used to buy items/accessories/weapons at Rodin's shop). All three totals are visible on-screen during gameplay at all times.
findings.trackable: All three currency totals are displayed persistently on the HUD (top-right corner), not hidden in a submenu.
sources: Search synthesis citing Samurai Gamers 'Seed Farming Guide', Inverse Halo farm guide, Gamer Journalist 'How to Find Halos'
findings.notes: Good candidate basis for a 'max out a currency' or 'reach X total' trophy since it's persistently visible, though exact HUD confirmation via direct screenshot/video was not independently done this pass (medium confidence).

findings.name: No confirmed randomized loot/drop-rate system
findings.detail: Treasure chests found across chapters appear to have FIXED, guide-documented contents (Broken Witch Hearts, Broken Moon Pearls, Golden LP record fragments at specific locations) rather than randomized loot tables - consistent with the franchise's history of hand-placed, skill-based progression rather than RNG loot. Currency drops (Halos/Orbs/Seeds) from enemies appear to scale with combo performance rather than random chance. No gacha-style mechanic was found for the 'Card Pack' collectible name notwithstanding - Card Packs are fixed world-placed collectibles unlocking specific Gallery art, not randomized packs.
findings.trackable: n/a - no RNG system to track
sources: Search synthesis across Nintendolife/Sportskeeda treasure chest guides, TheGamer/Nintendolife Card Pack guides
findings.notes: This is an absence-of-evidence finding, not a confirmed statement from a developer or comprehensive systems guide that 'there is no RNG in this game.' Recommend treating any trophy requiring RNG luck (e.g., 'get a rare drop') as unsupported by current evidence - the game appears to have essentially no relevant RNG systems for trophy design purposes.

findings.name: Platinum Ticket / Devil Rodin superboss (carried over from prior pass, re-confirmed relevant)
findings.detail: Post-game, spending 999,999 Homunculus Seeds on the 'Platinum Ticket' triggers a fight against Rodin at full power ('Devil Rodin'), described by at least one source as the toughest boss in the game. The 'Climax Earring' accessory (80,000 Seeds) grants infinite magic/Rage meter but disables score tracking while equipped - directly relevant to trophy design since equipping it would break any medal-rank-based trophy conditions.
findings.trackable: Presumably tracked via the accessories/shop menu (owned vs. not owned), not independently re-confirmed this pass.
findings.notes: Re-flagging because it's highly relevant to trophy design guardrails: any trophy requiring a Platinum/Pure Platinum medal must explicitly exclude runs with the Climax Earring equipped, since that accessory is documented to disable scoring.
